Synthesis and Rhodium(II)-Mediated Cascade Cyclopropanation/
Rearrangement/Isomerization of Diazo 2,3,5-Trisubstituted Furans:
The Construction of Penta-substituted Aromatic Compounds
Jianfang Zhang, Qin Yang, Yang Zhu, Jianbo Wang, and Guisheng Deng *
Cite This: J. Org. Chem. 2020, 85, 2395 −2405 Read Online
ACCESS Metrics & More Article Recommendations *sı Supporting Information
ABSTRACT: Ag(I)-catalyzed synthesis of diazo-trisubstituted furans starting from diazo-cumulated allenyl ketones has been
investigated. The Rh 2(OAc)4-catalyzed reaction of the diazo 2,3,5-trisubstituted furans provided penta-substituted aromatics via
cascade intermolecular cyclopropanation/rearrangement/isomerization. The cyclopropanation on the furan ring/rearrangement of
cyclopropane moiety has been reported. A reasonable mechanism is proposed.
1. INTRODUCTION
A diazo compound is a sort of important intermediates and have
been extensively employed as a carbene source in organic
synthesis. Many achievements have been made in the synthesis
and application of diazo compounds.
1−5 For example, the
functionalization of nonactivated C −H bonds, 6 cyclopropana-
tion reaction 7−9 (Scheme 1 a), and C(sp 2)−Hi n s e r t i o n
reaction10−15 (Scheme 1 b) has been described in literatures.
However, the cyclopropanation on the furan ring via metal
carbenoid has rarely been reported.
16 In fact, to the best of our
knowledge, synthetic application via the cyclopropanation has
never been reported.
In addition, penta-substitu ted aromatic compounds are
important intermediates in organic synthesis.
17 Synthesis of
the aromatic compounds has been widely explored, and many
achievements have been made.
18 However, they generally suﬀer
from some drawbacks such as multistep reactions. 19 Therefore,
the investigation on their simple and eﬃcient synthesis is always
underway.
Based on these considerations, a novel protocol for the
construction of penta-substituted aromatic compounds via a
selective cyclopropanation on the furan ring without the
corresponding C(sp
2)−H insertion is of interest. Herein, we
reported the synthesis of diazo-trisubstituted furans and their
application in the construction of penta-substituted aromatic
compounds (Scheme 1c).
2. RESULTS AND DISCUSSION
Diazo-cumulated allenyl ketones 1aa−1gb were easily prepared
by Michael reaction of α-alkynyl α,β-unsaturated ketones with
β-keto α-diazo carbonyl compounds based on the method
reported in literature. 20 The synthesis of diazo-trisubstituted
furans became our ﬁrst objective. For this goal, ethyl 6-benzoyl-
2-diazo-3-oxo-5,8-diphenylocta-6,7-dienoate 1aa was chosen as
the model substrate to establish a reaction system for the
construction of the furan cycle. 21
On the base of our previous research, 15 an initial plan for the
construction was to use Ag(I) compounds as the catalyst. In the
AgI (or AgSbF 6)/CH3CN/90 °C system, these attempts failed
(Table 1 , entries 1 −2). Happily, the utilization of AgNO 3
oﬀered the desired product 2aa, albeit in low yield ( Table 1 ,
entry 3). Other silver(I) compounds such as AgOAc,
CF
3CO2Ag, and AgBF 4 could also achieve the transformation
(Table 1 , entries 3 −6). In addition, the Pd(0) catalyst was
exploited as well. In the Pd(PPh3)4/THF/N2/25 °C system, the
product 2aa was indeed generated, but with accompany of the
formation of an unknown by-product (Table 1, entry 7). Among
all catalyst tested, CF3CO2Ag aﬀorded the best result in terms of
yield and cleanness of the reaction ( Table 1, entry 6).
In the CF 3CO2Ag (20 mol %)/25 °C system, the solvent
eﬀect on this reaction was examined to increase the yield (Table
1, entries 8 −12). The investigation of solvent revealed that the
highest yields (88%) were achieved in DCE ( Table 1, entry 9).
Reaction temperature also a ﬀected the reaction progress. As
expected, the elevation of reaction temperature facilitated to
shorten reaction time ( Table 1 , entries 13 −15). However, the
yield decreased at 80 °C, owing to the formation of unknown
side product ( Table 1, entry 15).
On the other hand, the eﬀect of catalyst loading of CF
3CO2Ag

corresponding products 2ab−2gb in yields of 75−85% (Table 2,
entries 11−17). In addition, we tried to expand the scope of the
reaction using designed substrates 1 (R3 = H, other alkyl or aryl;
R4 = H, alkyl or substituted phenyl), but the attempt was
unsuccessful because the preparation of these substrates has not
been reported in literature and has also been not achieved by us.
Next, we began the exploration of subsequent cycloaddition
process of diazo-trisubstituted furans 2. In theory, Rh
2(OAc)4-
mediated reaction of compound 2 could undergo Wol ﬀ
rearrangement and C(sp 2)−Hi n s e r t i o n ,15 providing the
corresponding products P-I, P-II and P-III (Figure 1). On the
basis of the protocol, we explored the possible cyclization
reaction of diazo-trisubstituted furans 2. Unfortunately, the
corresponding Wol ﬀ rearrangement and C(sp 2)−H insertion
products were not detected for all substrates examined by us.
Interestingly, in most cases, the reaction o ﬀered penta-
substituted aromatic compounds 4 or nonisomerization
products 3. These results arre illustrated in Table 3.
For substrates 2aa, 2fa, and 2ha−2ja (R
1 = Ph, p-FC6H4, n-
Bu, t-Bu, and H), the reaction gave the corresponding
nonisomerization products 3aa, 3fa, and 3ha−3ja (Table 3 ,
entries 1, 6, and 8−10). In the case of R2 = OEt, whether R1 is the
aryl group ( p-MeC4H4, p-MeOC4H4, p-BrC4H4, p-ClC4H4)o r
3-thienyl group, the only isomerization products 4ba−ea and
4ga were obtained without the corresponding nonisomerization
products 3ba−ea and 3ga (Table 3 , entries 2 −5 and 7). We
speculate that the aromatization of compounds 3ba−ea and 3ga
occurred more easily than that of compounds3aa, 3fa, and 3ha−
3ja. However, the reason is not clear at present.
When R 2 was changed into the phenyl group, the reaction
only a ﬀorded nonisomerization products 3ab−3cb, 3eb, and
3gb (Table 3 , entries 11 −13, 15, and 17). For substrates 2db
and 2fb (R1 = 3-thienyl and t-Bu), no desired products 3 and 4
were obtained, perhaps owing to both the steric e ﬀect of t-butyl
group and the electron e ﬀect of Ph group or 3-thienyl (R 2). In
the two cases, a mixture of complicated unknown side products
was only generated ( Table 3 , entries 14 and 16). In general,
when R
2 is Ar, the compound 3 is relatively stable because of the
existence of great π-conjugated system; in the case of R 2 = OEt,
the stability of product3 becomes weak. Thus, the aromatization
of the latter into the corresponding product 4 is easier to carry
out than that of the former. The structure of the penta-
substituted aromatic compound was ﬁnally established by
single-crystal X-ray di ﬀraction analysis of product 4ea (CCDC
1876455).
An attempt was made to transform compounds 3 into penta-
substituted aromatic compounds 4. An important in ﬂuence of
R
1 and R2 on the transformation was detected in the BF 3·OEt2/
DCM/25 °C system. These results are summarized inScheme 2.
In the case of R2 = OEt, the eﬀect of the substituent R1 on the
reaction was explored. The treatment of the substrate (3aa,R 1 =
Ph; 3fa,R 1 = p-FC6H4; 3ha,R 1 = n-Bu; 3ia,R 1 = t-Bu) gave the
corresponding penta-substituted aromatic compounds 4
(Scheme 2 , 4aa, 4fa, 4ha, and 4ia). In the case of R 2 = Ph, p-
FC6H4, and n-Bu, the conversion has been also achieved to oﬀer
the corresponding products ( Scheme 2 , 4ab, 4cb, and 4eb).
Obviously, the isomerization of compound (R 2 = Ph) 3 into 4
was more di ﬃcult than that in the case of R 2 = OEt, perhaps
owing to their exceptional di ﬀerence in stability.
Regretfully, when R2 is hydrogen, only a complicated mixture
of side products was formed under the standard conditions
(Scheme 2, 4ja and 4gb). In the case of R
1 = p-MeC6H4/R2 = Ph,
a similar result was observed ( Scheme 2 , 4bb). However, the
mechanism for the in ﬂuence of R 1 and R2 on the isomerization
reaction is not clear at present.
In addition, a possibility for one-pot synthesis of penta-
substituted aromatic compounds 4 starting from ethyl 6-acetyl-
2-diazo-3-oxo-5,8-diphenylocta-6,7-dienoate 1aa has been
exploited. In the Rh 2(OAc)4/CF3CO2Ag/BF3·OEt2/DCM/
N2/25 °C system, that is, under the optimal conditions for
above-mentioned step-by-step reaction, the one-pot reaction
only gave the corresponding furan derivative 2aa in 50% yield.
The conversion of 2aa into 3aa and 4aa did not occur, perhaps
because of the deactivation of Rh
2(OAc)4 in the system
(Scheme 3).

mechanism for the formation of cyclization products 4 starting
from trisubstituted furans 2 is depicted in Scheme 4. First, the

3. CONCLUSIONS
In conclusion, we have developed a novel method for the
synthesis of penta-substituted aromatic compounds starting
from diazo-cumulated allenyl ketones based on the domino
cyclopropanation/rearrangement/isomerization strategy. Other
noteworthy features of the cyclization reactions include
excellent chemoselectivity, mild reaction conditions, and simple
manipulation.

all signals are reported in ppm with the internal chloroform signal at
7.26 ppm. The data are being reported as (s = singlet, d = doublet, t =
triplet, q = quadruplet, m = multiplet or unresolved, br = broad signal).
